# Description

This course surveys federal and state laws governing employment, in both the individual and organized labor settings. Topics covered include the roots of employment and labor law; establishing an employment relationship; recruitment and hiring; supervisory control and employee autonomy; union representation and concerted activity; confidentiality and competition; wages and hours; employee health and safety; and termination of employment.

After completing the course, you should be able to recognize and diagnose legal issues arising in the employment context, analyze those issues under the applicable law, and help clients avoid legal problems or pursue remedies when they arise. Simulation problems and writing assignments provide opportunities to develop practical skills for representing clients in employment matters.

# Course Materials

## Required

Employment Law: An Open-Source Casebook (version 5.0, December 2026). Available on the course website: [emfink.net/EmploymentLaw](http://www.emfink.net/EmploymentLaw).  

Rachel Arnow-Richman & Nantiya Ruan, Developing Professional Skills: Workplace Law (West Academic 2017) ("Workbook"). 

## Suggested

Richard A. Bales, Jeffrey M. Hirsch, & Paul M. Secunda, Understanding Employment Law (4th. ed. Carolina Academic Press 2025)

# Policies

## Grading

Your final grade for this course will be based on two take-home writing assignments (30% each), peer assessment of contributions to group work (20%), and class participation (20%).[^syllabusABA] There will be no final exam.

### _Take-Home Assignments_ 

- I will provide instructions for each of these assignments at least one week before the due date (see _Schedule & Assignments_, below). You should submit each assignment to my faculty assistant, Jasmin Whitsett by email (jwhitsett4@elon.edu) or in person no later than 10:00am on the due date (see _Schedule & Assignments_ below). **Be sure to include your Exam ID number, _not your name_, at the top of your submissions.**
- The use of generative AI for take-home assignments is not permitted. The purpose of the assignments is to give you an opportunity to demonstrate what you have learned and what you can do. Among the many reasons to avoid artificial intelligence,[^syllabusAI] the most compelling is that it demeans your own intelligence.

### Group Work & Class Participation

- You will work in small groups on the practice simulation problems listed in the _Schedule & Assignments_ section of the syllabus. I will provide further information about this in class and will send instructions for each problem at least two days in advance of the scheduled date. 
- The class participation component of your grade will be based on your constructive engagement in class discussions. This will include presenting at least one question about the assigned reading each week. You should send your questions to me by email before the class for which the reading is assigned.

## Attendance

You should let me know (in advance if feasible) if you are unable to attend class, will arrive late, or must leave early. I do not require an explanation of the reason, nor do I require a doctor's note or other documentation. 

## Disability Accommodations

For disability accommodation requests, contact the [Office of Academic Accommodations and Accessibility](https://www.elon.edu/u/law/students/student-resources/academic-accommodations-accessibility/).

## Honor Code

The Law School [honor code](https://www.elon.edu/u/law/students/honor-code/) applies to all activities related to your law school study, including class meetings, assignments, and examinations.
